JordanGrayson Allen scored a career-high 42 points on 11/10 vs. NOP and set the franchise record for three-pointers (10).Last Game RecapOKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA – The Suns (45-37) concluded their 2025-26 regular season slate with a 135-103 win over the Thunder (64-18) on April 12. The 135 points marked a new season high, as the Suns recorded their 30th 45-plus wins season in franchise history. With the game tied at 5-5 a minute and a half into the game, Phoenix used a 21-0 run to build up a 26-5 lead with 4:36 remaining in the game. Phoenix’s lead never dropped below double figures the rest of the way. Phoenix led by 18 at halftime, finishing the season 18-0 when leading by 10 or more points at halftime. The Suns shot 55.4% from the field in the win, including a 20-of-41 mark from three-point range, while limiting the Thunder to 43.2% shooting. Jamaree Bouyea led the Suns offense with a career-high 27 points on 12-of-23 shooting, to go along with 9 assists, 5 rebounds, and 2 blocks. Ryan Dunn recorded his second double-double of the season and the fifth of his career, tallying 20 points on 8-of-11 shooting, 11 rebounds, and 5 assists. Rasheer Fleming matched his career-high in scoring with 16 points, 6 rebounds, 2 assists, and 2 steals, knocking down four of his seven three-point attempts. Amir Coffey got his first start with the Suns, totaling 17 points and 3 assists in the win. Koby Brea led all Suns reserves with a career-high 20 points on 7-of-11 shooting (6-of-9 3FG), 5 rebounds, and 3 assists in 29 minutes of play. Khaman Malauch posted a career-high 18 points and grabbed 14 rebounds off the bench, while CJ Huntley also scored a career-high 10 points off the bench.Play-In: The top six teams in each conference, ranked in order by win-loss records, qualify for the playoffs. – The Suns (0-1) fell to the Thunder (1-0) in their first game of the NBA Playoffs following a 119-84 loss on April 19. After Phoenix jumped out on a quick 5-0 run to begin the game, Oklahoma City responded with a 28-12 run to take an 11-point, 28-17, lead with 2:06 remaining in the first quarter. The Thunder lead remaining in double digits the rest of the way, extending up to as many as 39. OKC show 45.2% from the field to Phoenix’s 34.9% mark and turned 19 Suns turnovers into 34 points on the other end, while the Suns scored just 2 points off of 8 Thunder turnovers. Oklahoma City grabbed 19 offensive rebounds, leading to 25 second chance points and missed just two free throws on the night, finishing 21-for-23 from the charity stripe. Devin Booker scored a team-high 23 points, to go along with 6 rebounds and 2 assists. Dillon Brooks added 18 points, 7 rebounds, and 2 assists, while Jalen Green tallied 17 points and 5 rebounds.
